messages:
maya: FYI customer acme-inc reports sudden p95/p99 spike starting ~08:05 UTC, manifests as long request queueing and 504s. Link to request IDs: https://internal.logs/acme/reqs?since=08:00 :rotating_light:
alex: Thanks — any repro steps from the customer?
maya: They say it happens after a burst of parallel embeddings calls from a migration job. Provided snippet: `curl -X POST /v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"embed-400m","input":[...]}''` repeated ~200 concurrent.
sam: OK sounds like ingress admission kicking in. Can we confirm worker saturation on embed-400m shard pool?
jordan: Pulling metrics now — CPU on pool-embed-400m GPUs at 98%, queue depth at 420, inflight tokens jumping. p95 latency went from 120ms to 2.3s around 08:05.
ingress-bot: Alert: admit_queue_length>300 on pool-embed-400m (08:06:12) — backpressure engaged, response code 429 observed for some tenants.
oncall-bot: Runbook note: when queue depth>200, consider short-circuiting large-batch requests or enable soft-admit.
alex: Any change in recent deploys? CI shows no new runtime release in last 72h. Config change?
jordan: No runtime deploys. Found config tweak on ingress from yesterday: `admission.max_inflight: 100` applied to tenant wildcard override — might be too low relative to burst.
maya: Customer said they were migrating so concurrent count is higher than usual. We should reproduce locally with a scaled-down batch to confirm.
sam: Repro plan: 1) spin a small runner hitting /embeddings with 100 concurrent streams, 2) set model=embed-400m, 3) observe admit metrics and any 429s. I'll run now.
sam: (after 2m) Repro successful — incoming concurrency causes admission to kick, queue grows, downstream workers saturate and some requests time out. Logs: ```
2026-03-17T08:06:23Z ERROR admit: enqueue timeout tenant=acme shard=embed-400m queue_len=412
2026-03-17T08:06:27Z WARN worker: worker-s3-2 saturated in_kv=1.0
```

alex: Immediate mitigations? We can 1) increase admission.max_inflight for affected tenant, 2) enable request-shed-policy to fail fast for huge batch sizes, 3) route to a compatible lower-cost model temporarily.
jordan: I pushed a temp ingress override: `admission.max_inflight: 180` for tenant acme-inc in staging. Will promote to prod if a/b looks good.
maya: Also asked customer to pause the migration for 15m while we stabilize. They agreed. :thumbsup:

sam: Long-term: add tenant-based burst window detection and auto-burst scaling for embed pools, plus a per-tenant large-batch throttler that rewrites big parallel batch requests into smaller internal slices.
alex: For the immediate hotfix I'm going to roll a soft config bump to prod (+80 inflight) and enable request-size soft-shed rule to cap single request to 50 items. I'll coordinate the deploy.

alex: Deploy started (08:14). rolling update applying ingress-override v2 -> monitoring traces.
ingress-bot: Deploy ingress-override v2 started (08:15:03) — change: admission.max_inflight=180 for tenant=acme-inc.
jordan: After update: queue depth down to ~90 within 2m, p95 back to ~140ms, no further 504s.
maya: Customer confirm: their migration resumed at 08:22 and no more timeouts reported. They saw a few 429s during ramp but acceptable.
sam: Filing follow-up: ticket ops-5879 for engineering to implement burst policy + autoscale for embed pools. Also add guidance to docs for large-batch migrations.

alex: Postmortem quick notes: root cause = tenant-triggered burst > configured per-tenant inflight cap + insufficient burst capacity on embed-400m pool. Mitigation = temporary inflight cap bump + request-size soft-shed. Next steps assigned.
maya: I'll update the customer thread and close the escalation once ops-5879 links are created. Thanks team. :tada:
